In [[probability theory]], an '''exponentially modified Gaussian distribution''' ('''EMG''', also known as '''exGaussian distribution''') describes the sum of  independent [[Normal distribution|normal]] and [[Exponential distribution|exponential]] random variables. An exGaussian random variable ''Z'' may be expressed as {{nobr|''Z'' {{=}} ''X'' + ''Y''}}, where ''X'' and ''Y'' are independent, ''X'' is Gaussian with mean ''μ'' and variance ''σ''<sup>2</sup>, and ''Y'' is exponential of rate ''λ''. It has a characteristic positive skew from the exponential component.

It may also be regarded as a weighted function of a shifted exponential with the weight being a function of the normal distribution.

==Definition==
The [[probability density function]] (pdf) of the exponentially modified Gaussian distribution is<ref name="Grushka1972">{{cite journal |title=Characterization of Exponentially Modified Gaussian Peaks in Chromatography |last1=Grushka |first1=Eli|journal=Analytical Chemistry|volume=44|issue=11|pages=1733–1738|year=1972 |doi=10.1021/ac60319a011 |pmid=22324584}}</ref>

:<math>f(x;\mu,\sigma,\lambda) = \frac{\lambda}{2} \exp \left[\frac{\lambda}{2} (2 \mu + \lambda \sigma^2 - 2 x)\right]
             \operatorname{erfc} \left(\frac{\mu + \lambda \sigma^2 - x}{ \sqrt{2} \sigma}\right),
</math>

where erfc is the [[complementary error function]] defined as

:<math>\begin{align}
             \operatorname{erfc}(x) & = 1-\operatorname{erf}(x) \\
                                    & = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_x^\infty e^{-t^2}\,dt.
       \end{align}</math>

This density function is derived via [[convolution]] of the normal and [[Exponential distribution|exponential]] probability density functions.

==Alternative forms for computation==

An alternative but equivalent form of the EMG distribution is used to describe the shape of the peak in [[chromatography]].<ref name=Kalambet2011>{{Cite journal | last1 = Kalambet | first1 = Y. | last2 = Kozmin | first2 = Y. | last3 = Mikhailova | first3 = K. | last4 = Nagaev | first4 = I. | last5 = Tikhonov | first5 = P. | title = Reconstruction of chromatographic peaks using the exponentially modified Gaussian function | doi = 10.1002/cem.1343 | journal = Journal of Chemometrics | volume = 25 | issue = 7 | page = 352 | year = 2011 | s2cid = 121781856 }}</ref> This is as follows

{{NumBlk|:|<math id="1">
f(x; h, \mu, \sigma, \tau ) = \frac{h\sigma}{\tau} \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}}\exp \left( \frac {1}{2} \left( \frac {\sigma}{\tau} \right)^2 - \frac {x-\mu}{\tau} \right)  \operatorname{erfc} \left( \frac {1}{\sqrt{2}}\  \left( \frac {\sigma}{\tau}  - \frac {x-\mu}{\sigma} \right) \right ) ,
</math>|{{EquationRef|1}}}}

where
:<math>h</math> is the amplitude of Gaussian,
:<math id="1">\tau=\frac{1}{\lambda}</math> is exponent relaxation time, ''<math>\tau^2</math>'' is a variance of [[Exponential distribution|exponential]] probability density function.

This function cannot be calculated for some values of parameters (for example, <math>\tau=0</math>) because of arithmetic overflow. Alternative, but equivalent form of writing the function was proposed by Delley:<ref name="Delley1985">{{cite journal |title=Series for the Exponentially Modified Gaussian Peak Shape|last1=Delley|first1=R|journal=Anal. Chem.|volume=57|page=388|year=1985|doi=10.1021/ac00279a094}}</ref>

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
f(x; h, \mu, \sigma, \tau )=h\exp \left( -\frac {1}{2} \left( \frac {x-\mu}{\sigma} \right)^2\right)  \frac{\sigma}{\tau} \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}}\operatorname{erfcx} \left( \frac {1}{\sqrt{2}}\  \left( \frac {\sigma}{\tau}  - \frac {x-\mu}{\sigma} \right) \right ) ,
</math>|{{EquationRef|2}}}}

where <math> \operatorname{erfcx} t = \exp t^2 \cdot \operatorname{erfc} t</math> is a [[Error function|scaled complementary error function]]

For this formula, arithmetic overflow is also possible, but the region of overflow is different. 

For very small τ, an asymptotic form of the second formula can be used, which allows evaluation for <math>\tau=0</math>:

{{NumBlk|:|<math id="1">
f(x; h, \mu, \sigma, \tau )=\frac{h\exp \left( -\frac {1}{2} \left( \frac {x-\mu}{\sigma} \right)^2\right)}  
  {1+ \frac {\left(x-\mu\right)\tau}{\sigma^2}},
</math>|{{EquationRef|3}}}}

A decision on formula usage can be made on the basis of the parameter <math>z = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\frac{\sigma}{\tau} - \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}\right)</math>:
:for ''z'' < 0 computation should be made<ref name=Kalambet2011 /> according to the first formula,
:for 0 ≤ ''z'' ≤ 6.71·10<sup>7</sup> (in the case of [[double-precision floating-point format]]) according to the second formula, 
:and for ''z'' > 6.71·10<sup>7</sup> according to the asymptotic form of the second formula.
The [[Mode (statistics)|Mode]] (position of apex, most probable value) can be calculated<ref name=Kalambet2011 /> using the derivative of formula 2, where the inverse of [[Error function|scaled complementary error function]] erfcxinv() is used. Approximate values are also proposed by Kalambet et al.<ref name=Kalambet2011 /> Though the mode is at a value higher than that of the original Gaussian, the apex is always located on the original (unmodified) Gaussian.

==Parameter estimation==

There are three parameters: the [[mean]] of the normal distribution (''μ''), the [[standard deviation]] of the normal distribution (''σ'') and the [[exponential decay]] parameter (''τ'' = 1 / ''λ''). The shape ''K'' = ''τ'' / ''σ'' is also sometimes used to characterise the distribution. Depending on the values of the parameters, the distribution may vary in shape from almost normal to almost exponential.

The parameters of the distribution can be estimated from the sample data with the [[method of moments (statistics)|method of moments]] as follows:<ref name="google">{{cite book|title=Chromatographic Integration Methods|author=Dyson, N. A.|date=1998|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry, Information Services|isbn=978-0-85404-510-5|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=x8tGby300QMC|page=27|access-date=2015-05-15}}</ref><ref name=Olivier2010>Olivier J. and Norberg M. M. (2010) Positively skewed data: Revisiting the Box−Cox power transformation. Int. J. Psych. Res. 3 (1) 68−75.</ref>

: <math>m = \mu + \tau, </math>

: <math>s^2 = \sigma^2 + \tau^2, </math>

: <math>\gamma_1 = \frac{2\tau^3}{(\sigma^2 + \tau^2)^{3/2}}, </math>

where ''m'' is the sample mean, ''s'' is the sample standard deviation, and ''γ''<sub>1</sub> is the [[skewness]].

Solving these for the parameters gives:

: <math>\hat\mu = m - s \left( \frac{\gamma_1}{2} \right)^{1/3},</math>

: <math>\hat{\sigma^2} = s^2 \left[ 1 - \left( \frac{\gamma_1}{2} \right)^{2/3} \right],</math>

: <math>\hat\tau = s \left( \frac{\gamma_1}{2} \right)^{1/3}.</math>

===Recommendations===
Ratcliff has suggested that there be at least 100 data points in the sample before the parameter estimates should be regarded as reliable.<ref name=Ratcliff1979>{{cite journal | last1 = Ratcliff | first1 = R | year = 1979 | title = Group reaction time distributions and an analysis of distribution statistics | journal = Psychol. Bull. | volume = 86 | issue = 3| pages = 446–461 | doi=10.1037/0033-2909.86.3.446| pmid = 451109 }}</ref> [[Vincent average|Vincent averaging]] may be used with smaller samples, as this procedure only modestly distorts the shape of the distribution.<ref name=Vincent1912>{{cite journal | last1 = Vincent | first1 = S. B. | year = 1912 | title = The functions of the vibrissae in the behaviour of the white rat | journal = Animal Behaviour Monographs | volume = 1 | issue =5 | pages = 7–81 }}</ref> These point estimates may be used as initial values that can be refined with more powerful methods, including a least-squares optimization, which has shown to work for the Multimodal Exponentially Modified Gaussian (MEMG) case.<ref name=Hahne2022>{{cite book |doi=10.1109/IUS54386.2022.9958253 | arxiv = 2209.12202 | chapter = Multimodal Exponentially Modified Gaussian Oscillators | title = 2022 IEEE International Ultrasonics Symposium (IUS) | date = 2022 | last1 = Hahne | first1 = Christopher | pages = 1–4 | isbn = 978-1-6654-6657-8 }}</ref> A code implementation with analytical MEMG derivatives and an optional oscillation term for sound processing is released as part of an open-source project.<ref name="MEMG">{{Cite web|url=https://github.com/hahnec/multimodal_emg|title=MEMG on GitHub|website=[[GitHub]] }}</ref>

===Confidence intervals===
There are currently no published tables available for significance testing with this distribution. The distribution can be simulated by forming the sum of two random variables, one drawn from a normal distribution and the other from an exponential.

===Skew===
The value of the [[nonparametric skew]]

: <math> \frac{\text{mean} - \text{median}}{\text{standard deviation}} </math>

of this distribution lies between 0 and 0.31.<ref name=Heathcote1996>{{cite journal | last1 = Heathcote | first1 = A | year = 1996 | title = RTSYS: A DOS application for the analysis of reaction time data | journal = Behavior Research Methods, Instruments, & Computers | volume = 28 | issue = 3| pages = 427–445 | doi=10.3758/bf03200523| doi-access = free | hdl = 1959.13/28044 | hdl-access = free }}</ref><ref name=Ulrich1994>{{cite journal | last1 = Ulrich | first1 = R. | last2 = Miller | first2 = J. | year = 1994 | title = Effects of outlier exclusion on reaction time analysis | journal = J. Exp. Psych.: General | volume = 123 | issue = 1 | pages = 34–80 | doi=10.1037/0096-3445.123.1.34| pmid = 8138779 }}</ref> The lower limit is approached when the normal component dominates, and the upper when the exponential component dominates.

== Occurrence ==

The distribution is used as a theoretical model for the shape of [[Chromatography|chromatographic]] peaks.<ref name="Grushka1972" /><ref name=Kalambet2011 /><ref name="Gladney1969">{{cite journal |title=Computer-Assisted Gas-Liquid Chromatography|last1=Gladney|first1=HM|last2=Dowden|first2=BF|last3=Swalen|first3=JD|journal=Anal. Chem.|volume=41|issue=7|pages=883–888|year=1969|doi=10.1021/ac60276a013}}</ref> It has been proposed as a statistical model of [[Cell cycle|intermitotic time]] in dividing cells.<ref name="Golubev2010">{{Cite journal | last1 = Golubev | first1 = A. | title = Exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) relevance to distributions related to cell proliferation and differentiation | doi = 10.1016/j.jtbi.2009.10.005 | journal = Journal of Theoretical Biology | volume = 262 | issue = 2 | pages = 257–266 | year = 2010 | pmid =  19825376| bibcode = 2010JThBi.262..257G }}</ref><ref name="Tyson2012">{{Cite journal | last1 = Tyson | first1 = D. R. | last2 = Garbett | first2 = S. P. | last3 = Frick | first3 = P. L. | last4 = Quaranta | first4 = V. | title = Fractional proliferation: A method to deconvolve cell population dynamics from single-cell data | doi = 10.1038/nmeth.2138 | journal = Nature Methods | volume = 9 | issue = 9 | pages = 923–928 | year = 2012 | pmid =  22886092| pmc = 3459330}}</ref> It is also used in modelling cluster ion beams.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Nicolaescu | first1 = D. | last2 = Takaoka | first2 = G. H. | last3 = Ishikawa | first3 = J. | doi = 10.1116/1.2335433 | title = Multiparameter characterization of cluster ion beams | journal = Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology B: Microelectronics and Nanometer Structures | volume = 24 | issue = 5 | page = 2236 | year = 2006 | bibcode = 2006JVSTB..24.2236N }}</ref> It is commonly used in psychology and other brain sciences in the study of response times.<ref name=Palmer2011>{{cite journal | last1 = Palmer | first1 = EM | last2 = Horowitz Todd | first2 = S | last3 = Torralba | first3 = A |author4-link=Jeremy M. Wolfe | last4 = Wolfe | first4 = JM | year = 2011 | title = What are the shapes of response time distributions in visual search? | journal = J Exp Psychol | volume = 37 | issue = 1| pages = 58–71 | doi=10.1037/a0020747| pmid = 21090905 | pmc = 3062635 }}</ref><ref name=Rohrer1994>{{cite journal | last1 = Rohrer | first1 = D | last2 = Wixted | first2 = JT | year = 1994 | title = An analysis of latency and interresponse time in free recall | doi = 10.3758/BF03198390 | pmid = 7968547 | journal = Memory & Cognition | volume = 22 | issue = 5| pages = 511–524 | doi-access = free }}</ref> In a slight variant where the mean of the Normal component is set to zero, it is also used in [[Stochastic frontier analysis|Stochastic Frontier Analysis]], as one of the distributional specifications for the composed error term that models inefficiency.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Stochastic Frontier Analysis|last1=Lovell|first1=Knox CA|last2=S.C. Kumbhakar|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2000|pages=80–82|isbn=0-521-48184-8}}</ref> In signal processing, EMGs have been extended to the multimodal case with an optional oscillation term to represent digitized sound signals.<ref name=Hahne2022/>

==Related distributions==

This family of distributions is a special or limiting case of the [[normal-exponential-gamma distribution]]. This can also be seen as a three-parameter generalization of a normal distribution to add skew; another distribution like that is the [[skew normal distribution]], which has thinner tails. The distribution is a [[compound probability distribution]] in which the mean of a [[normal distribution]] varies randomly as a shifted [[exponential distribution]].{{citation needed|date=June 2023}}

A ''Gaussian minus exponential'' distribution has been suggested for modelling option prices.<ref>Peter Carr and Dilip B. Madan, Saddlepoint Methods for Option Pricing, The Journal of Computational Finance (49–61) Volume 13/Number 1, Fall 2009</ref>  If such a random variable ''Y'' has parameters ''μ'', ''σ'', ''λ'', then its negative ''-Y'' has an exponentially modified Gaussian distribution with parameters ''-μ'', ''σ'', ''λ'', and thus ''Y'' has mean <math>\mu - \tfrac{1}{\lambda}</math> and variance <math>\sigma^2 + \tfrac{1}{\lambda^2}</math>.
